skill.name: product-design-harness
skill.description: Review product directions, features, experiments, and launches before execution using evidence, stakeholder boundaries, and explicit decision gates.
skill.summary: Assess product decisions through User, Evidence, and Business Flow reviews before defining the next bounded action.
skill.author: cis2042

security_audit.summary: All 132 static alerts are false positives involving review terminology, Markdown references, schema identifiers, or ordinary API authentication in an unused helper. Two semantic findings identify review bypass and excessive implementation permissions in the standalone gate helper. No evidence found of credential theft, malicious exfiltration, or audit-directed prompt injection in the reviewed material.

remediation.issue: The route command emits bypass=true from routine keywords without validating scope, risk, or a prior approved review.
remediation.suggestion: Treat routing as advisory only. Require Quick Gate validation for routine changes and validated approval before emitting any execution authorization.

remediation.issue: The boundary helper grants implementation permissions for verify results and accepts unsupported evidence tiers without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate task inputs and evidence tiers. Handle verify separately with only its approved proof step, and require a validated review and context pack before implementation.

semantic_findings.title: Keyword Routing Can Bypass Required Review
semantic_findings.description: The route command emits bypass=true whenever routine keywords match and listed high-risk terms do not. Substring matching precedes the file-count check and cannot establish actual scope or risk. Consumers treating this output as authorization can skip the required review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly derives bypass from keyword routing, while SKILL.md retains review requirements for reversible changes. Harm depends on downstream consumers honoring bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Boundary Helper Grants Implementation Before Approval
semantic_findings.description: generate_boundary emits implementation permissions for verify results instead of limiting work to an approved proof step. It requires no validated review or context pack. Unsupported evidence tiers also fall through to continue, so unvalidated task data can produce misleading execution authorization.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Only stop_reframe has a separate boundary branch; verify reaches the implementation permission list. The documented contract explicitly forbids general coding under verify.

content.value_statement: Product teams can build features before testing the assumptions behind them. This skill structures evidence reviews and defines whether to continue, verify, or reframe.
actual_capabilities: Select Quick Gate, Standard Gate, or UX3 Council according to decision scope, uncertainty, and risk.
Review User Flow, Evidence Flow, and Business Flow using canonical questions and triggered rules.
Produce continue, verify, or stop_reframe verdicts with explicit next actions and execution boundaries.
Structure independent council reviews, challenge rounds, uncertainty checks, and human decision records.
Create bounded context packs for implementation after a continue verdict.
Validate review consistency, linked context packs, and verdict overrides with supplied Python validators.
limitations: Review quality depends on supplied evidence; simulations and opinions do not establish real user behavior.
Human owners must decide taste, ethics, strategy, and acceptable risk.
Python validation requires the supplied development dependencies and does not verify whether evidence is truthful.
The standalone gate helper can bypass review or permit implementation under verify; its output is not reliable execution authorization.

use_cases.title: Assess a Feature Proposal
use_cases.description: Compare stakeholder needs, evidence quality, and business viability before committing to a new feature.

use_cases.title: Plan Focused User Learning
use_cases.description: Identify the weakest assumption and define one bounded proof step before expanding a prototype.

use_cases.title: Constrain an Agent Handoff
use_cases.description: Turn an approved product review into a validated context pack with scope, approval gates, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Product Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product idea: [idea]. Select the smallest responsible review mode. Identify missing actors, evidence, and accountable owners. Do not implement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify a proposed product direction.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Standard Gate for [feature] using [evidence]. Review all three flows. List counter-evidence first. Return a canonical verdict and validate the review artifact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess a feature before committing resources.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Bounded Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this continue review: [review]. Create a context pack preserving its exact execution boundary and approval gates. Validate the linked artifacts before implementation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: transfer an approved decision to an execution agent.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a High-Risk Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Run UX3 Council for [decision] using [evidence]. Require independent lane reviews, challenges, and uncertainty checks. Add red-team review if all lanes continue. Record human-owned calls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: examine uncertain decisions with significant stakeholder impact.

output_examples.input: A product manager proposes automated exports based only on two customer requests.
output: Weakest flow: Evidence Flow; requests do not establish repeated workflow demand.
Next action: observe the existing export workflow with affected operators.
Boundary: run the proof step only; do not add scheduling or external delivery.

output_examples.input: A designer proposes a dashboard for everyone without a specific task or traceable evidence.
output: Weakest flow: Evidence Flow; no traceable signal supports the direction.
Reframed question: which operator repeatedly fails at which task?
Boundary: pause implementation and identify a concrete actor, situation, and current workaround.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead supplies a validated continue review for a bounded onboarding change.
output: Handoff: prepare a context pack linked to the approved review.
Scope: preserve the reviewed onboarding change and its acceptance criteria.
Restrictions: retain the review's data, stakeholder, and approval boundaries.
Stop condition: return to review if scope, affected people, or risk changes.

best_practices: Provide concrete actors, an accountable owner, traceable evidence, and counter-signals before requesting a verdict.
Validate review artifacts and linked context packs with the canonical validator before acting on them.
Keep verify work limited to its proof step and return to review when scope or risk changes.
anti_patterns: Treating simulations, isolated quotes, or confident summaries as validated behavioral evidence.
Averaging lane verdicts to conceal a weak flow or bypass a human-owned decision.
Using keyword routing or the standalone gate helper as permission to skip review or start implementation.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The package supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through its prompts, schemas, templates, and agent definitions.

faq.question: Does the skill implement features during review?
faq.answer: No. Review precedes execution. Implementation requires a continue verdict and a validated context pack.

faq.question: How do I choose a review mode?
faq.answer: Use Quick Gate for small reversible changes, Standard Gate for new workflows, and UX3 Council for uncertainty or significant risk.

faq.question: Can verify authorize general implementation?
faq.answer: No. Verify permits only the approved proof step. The standalone helper currently violates this boundary and must not serve as authorization.

faq.question: How are review outputs checked?
faq.answer: The supplied Python validator checks schemas, worst-verdict reduction, weakest-flow selection, evidence tiers, and linked handoff consistency.

faq.question: Does the command-line helper send data to an external API?
faq.answer: Its CLI branches do not call the API helper. Calling that helper separately would send state and questions to OpenRouter using OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
